title: Iran says no talks underway with US, sets conditions for future negotiations - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
AA - Iran said Monday that it is not currently engaged in negotiations with the US and that any future talks would depend on Washington changing its conduct.

Addressing a press briefing, Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baqaei dismissed reports that Tehran had sought negotiations with the US.

“That does not accord with our principles. Claims that Iran has requested negotiations are merely reports,” Baqaei said in his comments carried by the semi-official Mehr news agency.

He said Iran has consistently viewed diplomacy as a tool for safeguarding its interests.

“We have never hesitated to use diplomatic tools to protect our national interests. We consider diplomacy a means of protecting Iran's national interests,” he said.

While acknowledging that mediators may be conveying messages between the two sides, Baqaei said: “At the present time, we are not conducting any negotiations with the American side.”

Asked about Iran's conditions for starting negotiations, Baqaei said the US “must first demonstrate more responsible behavior.”

“The United States must learn how to behave like a responsible government,” he said, accusing Washington of acting “like a mafia gang” over the past one to two years by disregarding international law.

“As long as this behavior continues, we cannot hope to create a favorable public atmosphere,” he added.

On Sunday, Iranian military spokesperson Amir Mohammad Akraminia said the US had halted its attacks over the previous two days and that Iran's "counter-operations" had also stopped.

According to an Axios report on Saturday, US President Donald Trump had directed the US military not to launch new strikes on Iran, ending nearly two weeks of daily attacks.

Tensions between the US and Iran have intensified in recent weeks, with Washington carrying out attacks on Iran and Tehran responding by targeting what it said were US military facilities and equipment in countries across the region.

title: Bodies of five climbers found on Russia’s highest mountain - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Support the Guardian - Russia says it has found the bodies of five foreign climbers – believed to be Bosnian – on Mount Elbrus, authorities and state media say.

Authorities said earlier that out of a group of seven climbing Russia’s highest mountain, they had recovered two bodies and were searching for three more.

“According to investigators, on July 24 a group of seven climbers – foreign nationals – was climbing Mount Elbrus. The following evening, due to rapidly deteriorating weather conditions, the group strayed from the route,” the local prosecutor’s office said on Sunday.

It said one of the alpinists went down and told authorities that “two members of the group had fallen ill at an altitude of 5,100 metres and died”.

The statement added: “Subsequently, rescuers found another surviving climber and the bodies of three other climbers who had died.”

Bosnia’s foreign minister, Elmedin Konakovic, confirmed reports of the deaths, which he called “a major tragedy”.

Mount Elbrus, which rises to 5,642 metres just north of the border with Georgia, is infamous for sudden ⁠changes in weather and climbing conditions.

Bosnian media reported the seven members of the climbing expedition were residents of the central town of Zenica and included a married ‌couple and a female doctor who worked at the local hospital.

Russian media reported that adverse weather conditions including strong winds had complicated the search and recovery operations.

title: US, Sri Lanka launch CARAT 2026 maritime exercise - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 27 (Daily Mirror) - The United States and Sri Lanka have launched the sixth edition of the Cooperation Afloat Readiness and Training (CARAT) exercise, a bilateral maritime program aimed at strengthening cooperation in maritime security, humanitarian assistance, disaster response, and regional readiness.

Hosted by the Sri Lanka Navy in Trincomalee and Colombo from July 27 to 31, CARAT Sri Lanka 2026 brings together personnel from the U.S. Navy, U.S. Coast Guard, Sri Lanka Navy, and Sri Lanka Air Force for a week of shore- and sea-based training.

The exercise includes classroom sessions and practical training in maritime domain awareness, tactical medicine, explosive ordnance disposal, and visit, board, search and seizure (VBSS) operations before participants conduct joint activities at sea.

A U.S. Navy P-8A Poseidon maritime patrol and reconnaissance aircraft will support maritime surveillance training, while a U.S. Coast Guard Maritime Engagement Team will conduct training aboard SLNS Gajabahu (P626), the former U.S. Coast Guard Cutter Douglas Munro transferred to Sri Lanka by the United States. The team will also employ a U.S.-provided rigid-hull inflatable boat during maritime operations.

U.S. Embassy Senior Defense Official and Defense Attaché to Sri Lanka, Lt. Col. Matthew House, said the exercise reflects the United States' enduring commitment to its security partnership with Sri Lanka.

"When our sailors train side-by-side, they build the trust, interoperability, and professional relationships that allow us to respond more effectively together when it matters most," he said.

In addition to operational training, the exercise includes community service projects, sporting events, and cultural exchanges designed to strengthen ties between service members.

The annual CARAT exercise, held in Sri Lanka since 2017, is aimed at enhancing interoperability between the two countries' armed forces and improving their ability to respond jointly to maritime security challenges, search and rescue missions, natural disasters, and other regional threats in the Indian Ocean.

title: Strong winds forecast over several areas; public urged to take precautions - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
By Mangala Pavithrani

Colombo, July 27 (Daily Mirror) - The Department of Meteorology has issued a warning of strong winds over several parts of the country and the surrounding sea areas due to active southwest monsoon conditions.

The warning, issued at 11.00 a.m. today (July 27), is valid for 24 hours until 11.00 a.m. on July 28.

The department said wind speeds of 40 to 50 km/h may occur at times in the Northern, North Central and Central provinces, as well as in the Hambantota and Trincomalee districts.

The strong winds could damage roof tiles, power and telephone lines, and cause tree branches or even large trees to fall, posing a risk to people and property. Crop damage is also possible, while low-lying coastal areas may experience sea wave inundation.

Meanwhile, wind speeds in the sea areas from Hambantota to Pottuvil and from Kalpitiya to Kankesanthurai via Mannar may increase to 50 to 60 km/h at times, making these sea areas very rough. Vessels anchored near harbours could also be be at risk of damage due to collisions.

The department has advised the public, fishermen and naval communities to take the necessary precautions and follow the recommended safety measures to minimise the risk of accidents caused by the strong winds.

title: Colombo University signs MoU with Sri Lanka Inventors Commission to boost innovation - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 27 (Daily Mirror) - The University of Colombo has signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with the Sri Lanka Inventors Commission (SLIC) to strengthen innovation, entrepreneurship, and the commercialization of research.

The agreement aims to enhance support for student entrepreneurs and researchers by combining the University's academic expertise with SLIC's national experience in inventions and innovation.

Under the partnership, the University's newly established Innovation & Startup Incubator will receive support in curriculum development, intellectual property advisory services, industry mentorship, and access to funding networks to help transform research into commercially viable solutions.

The MoU was signed by University of Colombo Vice Chancellor Professor Indika Mahesh Karunathilake and SLIC Commissioner Professor Veranja Karunaratne in the presence of representatives from both institutions.

University officials said the collaboration reflects the institution's commitment to fostering a strong innovation ecosystem that will benefit students, researchers, and Sri Lanka's broader innovation landscape.

title: Rs. 200,000 paid to shoot Dehiwala Cemetery guard; Gunman arrested - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 27 (Daily Mirror) - Police have arrested the alleged gunman involved in the shooting of a security guard at the Nisala Sewana public cemetery in Dehiwala-Mount Lavinia, Deputy Inspector General (DIG) of Police for the Colombo District, Nishantha de Zoysa, said today (27).

The shooting took place on July 19 when two men arrived on a scooter-type motorcycle and opened fire on the cemetery guard before fleeing the scene. The attackers allegedly used a 9mm firearm.

The victim, a 56-year-old resident of the Dehiwala Fishermen's Housing area, sustained gunshot injuries to his left arm and chest and was admitted to the Kalubowila Teaching Hospital for treatment.

Police had earlier arrested the motorcycle rider in the Delkanda area on July 26. During the arrest, officers recovered 7 grams and 200 milligrams of crystal methamphetamine ("Ice") from the 25-year-old suspect.

According to police, investigations revealed that the shooting had been carried out on the instructions of an organized criminal believed to be hiding overseas. The suspects had allegedly been promised Rs. 200,000 to carry out the attack.

Police also recovered Rs. 55,000, believed to be part of the payment for the shooting, along with three mobile phones allegedly used by the suspect during the operation.

Investigations into the incident are continuing.

title: Rupee weakens slightly against US Dollar - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 27 (Daily Mirror) - The Sri Lankan Rupee depreciated slightly against the US Dollar today (27), according to the latest exchange rates released by the Central Bank of Sri Lanka.

The buying rate of the US Dollar rose marginally from Rs. 331.62 last Friday to Rs. 331.66, while the selling rate increased from Rs. 340.79 to Rs. 340.83.

The Rupee also weakened against a basket of major foreign currencies but recorded slight gains against several Gulf currencies, the Central Bank's exchange rates showed.

title: Horana tuition centre owner arrested with crystal meth - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 27 (Daily Mirror) - The owner of a private tuition centre in Horana has been arrested for allegedly possessing the narcotic drug known as "Ice" (crystal methamphetamine), police said.

The suspect, a 44-year-old resident of the Narthanagala area in Horana, was taken into custody during a police raid at his residence.

Police said they recovered 15g 250mg of crystal methamphetamine from the suspect's possession. Officers also seized a mobile phone, a SIM card believed to have been used for drug trafficking activities, and an electronic weighing scale.

According to investigators, the suspect attempted to flee when police arrived at his residence but was apprehended after a brief pursuit.

Preliminary investigations have revealed that the suspect is the son of a well-known businessman in the Horana area. Police further said that he has previously faced several drug-related charges.

Police are also probing whether the suspect had links to organized drug trafficking networks, operated a wider drug distribution operation, and whether narcotics were supplied to students attending his tuition classes.

title: Former State Minister Shantha Bandara’s son granted bail - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 27 (Daily Mirror) - Five suspects, including Anuda Janadith Bandara, the son of former State Minister Shantha Bandara, have been granted bail by the Fort Magistrate’s Court in connection with the alleged robbery of Rs. 20 million belonging to a Chinese national.

Fort Magistrate Pasan Amarasena ordered the release of the suspects on personal bail of Rs. 500,000 each and imposed a travel ban preventing them from leaving the country.

Bandara and the four other suspects were arrested on July 21 over allegations that they robbed Rs. 20 million from a Chinese national.

title: Very happy if BASL issues statement on Wijeyadasa or his son: Chathuranga - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 27 (Daily Mirror) - Deputy Minister Chathuranga Abeysinghe said he would be "very happy" to see the Bar Association of Sri Lanka (BASL) issue a statement regarding former Justice Minister Wijeyadasa Rajapakshe or his son, questioning whether the association applies the same standards in all cases.

Whike speaking to the media, Abeysinghe said such a move would help determine whether the BASL was acting independently or protecting a particular group.

"We will see whether this is genuine or whether these actions are being taken to protect one particular class," he said.

Abeysinghe also confirmed that the Government intends to bring Constitutional amendments to increase the retirement age of judges.

He said a Constitutional amendment would be required for changes affecting the judiciary, while other reforms could be introduced at Ministerial level.

title: Shooting at U.S. Seattle food festival leaves 2 dead, wounds 5
summary: Two people were killed, and five others were wounded in a shooting on Sunday (July 26, 2026) evening during a food festival at an events complex near the Space Needle in Seattle, a city fire department spokesperson said.

title: Three-wheeler driver killed in Gothatuwa road accident - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 27 (Daily Mirror) - A three-wheeler driver was killed in a road accident in the Gothatuwa area this morning (27), Police said.

The accident occurred when a three-wheeler travelling from Kolonnawa towards Gothatuwa collided with a private bus.

The three-wheeler driver died at the scene, while another person who sustained injuries was admitted to the Colombo National Hospital for treatment.

Kolonnawa Police are conducting further investigations into the incident.

title: AI will take away SL’s business outsourcing revenue: MP - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 27 (Daily Mirror) - Indicating that artificial intelligence (AI) will affect Sri Lanka's economy in an unimaginable way, Opposition MP Ravi Karunanayake said it has already begun to take away the revenue which the country has been generating out of business process outsourcing.

"The emergence of AI has already made one company engage in providing business process outsourcing service to reduce salaries for its employees," he added.

Also, the MP said the reduction in Sri Lanka's birth rate will have a negative effect on the country.

"The fact of the matter is that Sri Lanka's aging population will increase as a result of the reduced birth rate, which is even less than one percent. Sri Lanka will have to face certain social and economic issues with the increase of the aging population," he said.

Furthermore, he said Sri Lanka should focus on energy security in the wake of hostilities in the Middle East.

"Sri Lanka should focus on making the rupee stable so that the increase of oil prices will be manageable with a stable local currency."

"Another fact which the country should focus is power. There could be a high demand for renewable energy later this year and early next year with the El Nino phenomenon which is expected to hit Sri Lanka. Sri Lanka should focus on renewable energy in that scenario," the MP also said.

title: Colombo sees over 250 fire incidents so far this year - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 27 (Daily Mirror) - A total of 258 fire incidents have been reported in Colombo and its surrounding areas during this year, the Fire Service Department has revealed.

According to the Department, 17 rescue operations were carried out in connection with these fire incidents during the same period.

Officials noted that 382 fire incidents were recorded in the Colombo District throughout last year, along with 46 rescue operations.

The Department stressed that the fact that 258 fire incidents have already been reported in the Colombo District from January to date this year is a matter that warrants serious attention.

In addition to fire-related incidents, the Fire Service Department has also responded to 13 emergency calls so far this year.

These included rescue operations related to road obstructions, fallen trees, and road traffic accidents.

The Department said investigations have identified several key factors contributing to the rise in fire incidents, including the lack of adequate fire safety measures at workplaces, failure to respond promptly to emergencies, unsafe electrical installations and practices in homes and commercial premises, and the prevailing dry weather conditions.

title: Seek prompt medical treatment if children’s fever persists over 24 hours: Health authorities - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 27 (Daily Mirror) - In the wake of growing risk of dengue spread, Health authorities urged parents to seek prompt medical treatment without delay, if children's fever persists for more than 24 hours.

Director at the Lady Ridgeway Hospital for Children in Colombo, Dr. Pradeep Ratnasekara advised parents not to resort to unscientific home remedies claiming that staying at home and using home remedies wastes the time available to treat the child.

He urged parents to take the child to the nearest government hospital and seek proper medical advice.

Dr. Ratnasekara said around 50 children infected with dengue are currently receiving treatment at the Lady Ridgeway Hospital and that about one-fourth of them are in critical condition.

He said if this situation worsens further, issues regarding hospital capacity could arise.

"I must particularly state that it is not necessary to bring your child to the Lady Ridgeway Hospital all the way from distant areas. The main reason for many deaths is late arrival at the hospital. If a fever persists for more than 24 hours, it is appropriate to seek medical advice. Instead of staying at home for days doing home remedies and wasting your valuable time along with the time required to provide the necessary treatment for the child, it is extremely important to bring them to a qualified doctor or a government doctor very quickly," he said.

He said only one dengue death has been reported in the Lady Ridgeway Hospital.
